claims.text: Uniaxial tensile and compression testing can be used to characterize the mechanical properties of as-cast FeNiCrMn HEA.
As-cast FeNiCrMn will exhibit strength and ductility different from those of the Co-containing Cantor alloy.
Any predicted strength and ductility differences are attributable to removing Co.
The FeNiCrMn HEA is produced in an as-cast condition by conventional melting methods.
As-cast FeNiCrMn has a single solid-solution phase similar to Co-containing HEAs.
Mechanical testing should be conducted at room temperature and elevated temperature.
SEM and TEM characterization can be combined with mechanical testing to examine the microstructure.
The selected elevated temperatures are representative of potential aerospace and automotive applications.
Grain size, phase homogeneity, and lattice distortion govern dislocation mobility in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Eliminating Co alters atomic-size mismatch and lattice distortion.
Changes in atomic-size mismatch and lattice distortion modify dislocation interactions.
Modified dislocation interactions affect the balance between yield strength and ductility.
FeNiCrMn should retain outstanding corrosion resistance.
FeNiCrMn may show slightly reduced ductility or modified strengthening relative to the Cantor alloy.
The CoCrFeMnNi Cantor alloy has a well-studied combination of tensile strength and elongation.
Thermomechanical processing may further alter the properties of FeNiCrMn.
The magnitude and direction of the strength–ductility shift caused solely by Co elimination are uncertain.
HEAs can exhibit complex interactions that complicate prediction of mechanical behavior.
An as-cast FeNiCrMn test series can be prepared by arc melting and tested at room temperature and approximately 600 °C.
Statistically indistinguishable mechanical properties and no significant microstructural differences relative to the Cantor alloy would falsify the proposed significant effect of Co removal.
